_concept: PROCESS FLOWS — the layer the module axis cannot express
_one_line: A component is what SAP built. A domain is who owns it. A FLOW is what the organisation actually does end to end — and it crosses both.

_why.the_defect: The model keyed domains on SAP modules — FI, CO, MM, SD. That is a TECHNICAL
taxonomy wearing a business name. No one in the organisation does 'FI'. They pay
an invoice, commit a budget, or hire a person, and every one of those crosses
_why.the_second_defect: `_module_to_domain` was ONE-TO-ONE. It cannot be. The same component
serves several flows: FI-BL-PT (payment transactions) pays suppliers in
P2P, pays staff in payroll, reimburses travellers, and settles treasury
deals. Forcing it into one domain either loses three flows or invents a
_why.why_the_market_does_it_this_way: Celonis and Signavio ship content named P2P, O2C, R2R —
PROCESS names, never module names. Their unit of analysis is
the flow because that is the unit a business recognises and
the unit a deviation is measured against.
_why.consequence: Process mining must run on FLOWS. A DFG built per module produces a picture
nobody can act on; a DFG built per flow produces a process map with a normative

_layers.1_COMPONENT: SAP's own taxonomy (FI-BL-PT-BS-EL). Deterministic, resolved via TADIR→TDEVC→DF14L. We do not invent it and we do not rename it.
_layers.2_DOMAIN: an area of business responsibility — who owns the data and the decisions. Several components, and a component may serve more than one.
_layers.3_FLOW: an end-to-end chain the organisation performs. Crosses domains and components. THIS is the unit of process mining and of conformance.
_layers._cardinality: component ↔ domain is MANY-TO-MANY. domain ↔ flow is MANY-TO-MANY. Anything modelled as 1:1 between these layers is a modelling error, not a simplification.

_market_reference._note: Where this comes from. We adopted the field's method and are extending it — not inventing a parallel vocabulary.
_market_reference.engine: pm4py — the reference implementation of the discipline (van der Aalst lineage), the same substrate Celonis and Signavio productised
adopted: declarative conformance against a normative reference
OCEL 2.0 object-centric event logs — one event referencing MULTIPLE object types, no forced single-case notion
_market_reference.our_extension: the market's normative content stops at commercial flows. The public-sector
flows below have no vendor content at all, and they are where the customer's

P2P.name: Procure to Pay
P2P.normative_reference: 3-way match; goods receipt strictly BEFORE invoice receipt
P2P.public_sector_twist: the commitment check against available budget (AVC) sits between requisition and PO — absent from every commercial reference model

B2C2A.name: Budget to Commitment to Actual
B2C2A.normative_reference: no commitment may exceed available budget; every actual must trace to a commitment or an explicit exception
B2C2A.why_it_matters: this is the public-sector equivalent of R2R and it is the organisation's primary financial control. FMRESERV alone carries 6.4M change documents.
B2C2A.gap: no event log, no DFG, no conformance model. The most important flow in the tenant is unmined.

POST2BUDGET.name: Post to Budget (position budgeting)
POST2BUDGET.normative_reference: every established post carries a funded commitment before payroll executes
POST2BUDGET.why_it_matters: staff cost is the largest budget line in a UN agency. 68 users touch it directly — the widest dialog audience measured.
POST2BUDGET.gap: the engine runs daily and nothing mines it

PROJ2FUND.name: Project to Fund
PROJ2FUND.normative_reference: every WBS consuming budget derives to exactly one fund; derivation is deterministic and auditable
PROJ2FUND.why_it_matters: PS is the busiest business domain in the tenant (1.6M executions) and its whole point is consuming budget
PROJ2FUND.gap: PS has zero knowledge documents. The busiest flow is the least understood.

GRANT2REPORT.name: Grant to Report
GRANT2REPORT.normative_reference: expenditure must satisfy sponsor eligibility rules before posting
GRANT2REPORT.status: NOT USED at UNESCO (GMGR = 0 rows, measured) — and almost certainly used by peer organisations
GRANT2REPORT.gap: no capability at all. Cheap to ignore here; expensive to discover on the second client.

H2R.name: Hire to Retire
H2R.public_sector_twist: the post must be funded before the hire — POST2BUDGET gates this flow

O2C_BILLING.name: Order to Invoice (billing-only)
O2C_BILLING.market_content: yes, but the standard reference assumes delivery
O2C_BILLING.deviation_from_reference: ZERO deliveries measured — this tenant runs order→invoice with no logistics execution. A standard O2C reference model would report 100% non-conformance, which would be a false finding.

DISBURSE.name: Approve to Disburse
DISBURSE.normative_reference: dual control on release; every disbursement reconciles to a bank statement
DISBURSE.why_it_matters: 3.7M payment records; segregation of duties is the live control question
implemented: partial — BCM dual-control audit exists as a companion, not as a mined flow

_component_serves_many_flows._note: The evidence for the many-to-many claim. Each of these components appears in several flows above; a 1:1 module→domain map cannot express any of it.

_naming_decision.question: Should the domains be renamed to match components?
_naming_decision.answer: NO — and the question reveals the real fix. Domains should NOT be renamed to component
codes; that would deepen the confusion by making a business layer look technical.
Instead: KEEP the component layer as SAP names it (it is theirs and it is
deterministic), keep domains as ownership areas, and ADD this flow layer as the unit
of process analysis. Three layers with honest many-to-many edges, rather than one
layer pretending to be all three.
what_changes_in_practice: process mining runs per FLOW, never per module
conformance is measured against a flow's normative reference
a domain answers 'who owns this', a flow answers 'what happens'
the capability model keeps its domain rows; flows get their own coverage
